label: Continuous clearing auction
summary: Define continuous or discrete clearing-price discovery with explicit deposits, fills, refunds and settlement invariants.
requiredFacts: Auction opening, closing, tick, epoch and clearing rules including exact time and block sources
Bid or order commitment, deposit, cancellation, partial fill, finalization, refund and claim lifecycle
Clearing-price math, rounding, tie breaking, minimums, caps and unsold-inventory treatment
Who can finalize, pause or recover an auction and the liveness path when automation fails
Transition from auction accounting into canonical-pool liquidity and ordinary trading
requiredFiles: Bid, refund and claim lifecycle specification
requiredTests: Clearing-price differential tests against an independent reference model
Zero, one, tied, oversubscribed, undersubscribed and boundary-price order books
Deposit conservation across fills, refunds, claims, rounding and unsold inventory
Late, duplicate, censored, reordered and adversarial finalization behavior
MEV, timestamp, block-ordering, sandwich and last-look manipulation scenarios
risks: Clearing or rounding errors can misprice every participant in an epoch
Finalizer liveness or ordering power can censor, delay or manipulate outcomes
Auction-to-pool transition errors can strand inventory or create discontinuous pricing
